name: Willie Soon

summary.text: Willie Wei-Hock Soon is an astrophysicist who worked at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics and published papers questioning the human role in climate change. Documents obtained by Greenpeace through public-records requests, reported in February 2015, showed about $1.25 million in funding from ExxonMobil, the American Petroleum Institute, Southern Company and a Koch foundation, with Southern Company given a right to review papers before publication; many of the papers did not disclose the funding. Soon said the funders did not influence his work. Peabody Energy's 2016 bankruptcy creditor list also named him.

facts.claim: Correspondence with funders described Soon's papers and testimony as 'deliverables', and at least 11 papers published since 2008 did not disclose any connection to the companies that paid him.

facts.claim: Soon and the Harvard-Smithsonian Center gave Southern Company the right to review his scientific papers and make suggestions before publication; Southern Company's research grants totalled $409,754 between 2006 and 2015.
facts.quote: Soon and Harvard-Smithsonian gave the coal utility company the right to review his scientific papers and make suggestions before they were published

facts.claim: Greenpeace's 2011 analysis listed at least $175,000 from Koch family foundations, $230,000 from Southern Company, $274,000 from the American Petroleum Institute and $335,000 from ExxonMobil; the Charles G. Koch Foundation grants were two totalling $175,000, in 2005/6 and 2010.
facts.quote: The Charles G. Koch Foundation figures are also given as two grants totaling $175,000, in 2005/6 and again in 2010.

facts.claim: Soon acknowledged receiving money from the groups and companies named but denied that any of them influenced his studies.
facts.quote: Soon told Reuters that he agreed that he had received money from all of the groups and companies named in the report but denied that any group would have influenced his studies.
